signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Policy Decision + Volatility Premium
signals.text: The BoE holds at 3.75%. GBP/USD trades at 1.3361, sitting within a dense moving average cluster where the SMA50 at 1.3364 provides immediate support and the SMA20 at 1.3381 caps the upside. Options markets are pricing in significant event risk, with GBP/USD ATM IV at 11.0% vs an HV30 of 6.2%, creating a massive +4.8% Vol Risk Premium. COT data shows leverage funds remain net long +33,812, making the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if the BoE delivers a dovish hold. The current bear steepener regime in US yields (+36.2bp 2s10s) provides a stable backdrop for the USD, limiting cable's recovery potential. Risk: A hawkish BoE surprise or clear commitment to future hikes triggers a squeeze through the SMA200 at 1.3398.

signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5823 represents the dominant G10 theme this week as the NZD outperforms all peers by an average of +0.600%. The leader-to-laggard spread between NZD (+0.600%) and USD (-0.334%) has reached 0.934% across 7 pairs, triggering a bilateral G10 theme alert. Despite a 125bp carry disadvantage (Fed 3.75% vs RBNZ 2.5%), the pair is supported by a strong NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +30.6, contrasting with the neutral USD ESI of -0.8. Speculative positioning remains an extreme contrarian tailwind, as leverage funds are net short -31,649 (long% only 12.0%), suggesting a massive short-squeeze is underway. Price is currently testing the SMA200 at 0.5825; a sustained break above this level confirms a trend reversal. Risk: A cooling of RBNZ hike expectations in the next meeting cycle halts the NZD outperformance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY at 163.58 remains supported by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (3.75% vs 1.0%), though technical and options data signal caution. The pair is trading well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (162.61/161.33/157.89), reflecting the persistent long-term uptrend. However, the options market is paying up for downside protection, with the 25d Risk Reversal showing a strong -1.55 put skew, the most extreme in the G10 space. This negative skew suggests institutional desks are hedging against BoJ intervention or a carry unwind despite the nominal rate advantage. Retail sentiment is also extreme at 81% short, diverging from the leverage fund net short of -114,030, which indicates retail traders are unsuccessfully trying to fade the move. Risk: A break below the SMA20 at 162.61 triggers a forced liquidation of carry positions.

signals.title: AUD/USD — ESI Underperformance vs Accommodative Real Rates
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6965, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster at 0.6968/0.7017. The pair faces fundamental headwinds from the G10's weakest data pulse, with the AUD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) at -16.7 following persistent misses. While the RBA holds a 60bp nominal carry advantage (4.35% vs 3.75%), high inflation expectations of 5.50% result in an accommodative real policy rate of -1.15%, compared to the USD real rate of +1.51%. This 266bp real rate differential favors the USD and explains the AUD's inability to capitalize on its nominal yield. Speculative positioning is moderately long (lev_net +20,521), but further data misses threaten to turn this positioning into a source of supply. Risk: Upcoming RBA meeting on 11 Aug shifts to a more aggressive hiking stance to combat the negative real rate.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break vs WTI Oil
signals.text: USD/CAD at 1.4057 is exhibiting a significant correlation break with WTI Oil, with the current correlation at -0.907 vs a 252-day norm of -0.024 (z = -1.57σ). While WTI is up +0.65% on the session at $85.0, USD/CAD has failed to weaken, staying bid due to the 150bp USD carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.25%). Leverage funds are heavily positioned for CAD weakness with a net short of -99,823 (long% 18.8%), nearing historical extremes. Price is currently trapped between the SMA50 at 1.4041 and the SMA20 at 1.4114, suggesting a period of consolidation despite the oil market volatility. Risk: A reversal in the USD carry trade or a sharp spike in oil prices above $90 forces a covering of the crowded CAD short.
